literature_notes: All four ledger clips (L1–L4) describe the identical construct: full-length human XEDAR/EDA2R with EGFP fused at the C-terminus (XEDAR-GFP). Per the authoritative topology landmarks, EDA2R is a Type I single-pass receptor: extracellular N-terminal domain residues 1–139, TM 140–160, intracellular C-tail 161–297. The C-terminus (residue 297) therefore lies on the cytoplasmic face. The C-terminal GFP fusion is tolerated and functional (L2: construct responds to EDA-A2 ligand), but it is an intracellular tag, not an extracellular surface tag. No ledger line reports any insertion in the extracellular domain (residues 1–139) or at the extracellular N-terminus. Because the ledger provides zero evidence for an extracellular tag on EDA2R, sites = [].

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal EGFP fusion (XEDAR-GFP) is explicitly constructed at the C-terminus (residue 297), which is intracellular (topology residues 161–297); the tagged construct is stably expressed and functionally responsive to EDA-A2 (L2), but the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
